3.4.1; core/README.md's contract). Every test case in every suite file
wired into vitest.core-suites.config.ts's `test.include` is listed here,
classified as one of:
- "portable":     runs on the core for the kinds it uses; wired into
vitest.core-suites.config.ts's testNamePattern.
- "classic-only":  pins a classic-internal detail (step counts, Newton
iteration counts, engine.state, captureErrorState,
a split) that has no core counterpart and is not
part of the accuracy contract; never runs on the core.
- "not-yet":       every kind the test's circuit uses is real device
behaviour, but at least one of those kinds has not
been ported to the core yet (or, for a handful of
kinds below, is not in the W1 plan's kind table at
all -- diode/bjt_npn/nmos/lm358/microbit).
`kinds` lists every SimComponent.kind the test's circuit instantiates
(excluding the implicit ground net). gate-reporter.ts sums, per kind, how
many "portable" cases actually ran and passed under this file's
testNamePattern, and fails the whole run if any kind named in a portable
case's `kinds` array has a count of zero for that file -- see its own
header comment for why this must be computed from portable entries only,
not from CORE_IMPLEMENTED_KINDS (which also contains "ground", a compiler-
internal detail no test ever names as a component kind). It ALSO fails
when any CORE_IMPLEMENTED_KINDS member except "ground" has no portable
case, in any file, that ran and passed (the coverage floor, W1b review
finding 9): a kind the core implements must be exercised here.
W1e added suite files that mix cases of every kind. For those, only the cases that build one of the six W1e kinds (led, rgb_led,
bicolor_led, seg7_cc, seg7_ca, ne555) are listed; their other cases are unlisted, so the core project never collects them, and are
classified in the wave that ports the kinds they need. The gate-1 checks above apply to what is listed.

The core's single-capacitor partition (W1b step 2) advances the closed form continuously (no per-step h to reconstruct a matching discrete derivative from), so this identity is not a like-for-like comparison there. A future worker could add that passthrough (HeadlessRunnerOptions.compileOptions, threaded into CoreEngine.load's options) to lift this to "portable" under FORCE_STEPPED.

cases.describe: spdt_switch.updateCurrent — Q-O26 (com to the contact in use)
cases.name: position 0 (com->b active, b floating with no load) reports ~0 A: no complete circuit
cases.reason: com is fixed (wired directly to the source) and b is the device's only OTHER free pin (c has no wire to it either in this case's own rig, since r1 sits on c) -- wait, r1 is wired to c even here, so b and c are the device's two free contacts in potentially different partitions (com fixed, so nothing unions them, per finding 1). cases.describe: capacitor ESR + leakage backward-Euler companion
cases.name: applies exact catalog ESR/leakage defaults to an older identified save
cases.reason: This fixture's capacitor sits directly across the ideal source (c.a to src.pos, c.b to src.neg) -- BOTH terminals are fixed nodes, and rule 2a (core/README.md) now gives the core an exact closed form for exactly this topology instead of declining it, so the old topology block is gone. But this specific test is not a rule-2a check: it hand-computes ONE deliberately huge backward-Euler step (h=0.5s against esr=1, C=1F -- h/(esr*C) = 0.5, half of tau) and asserts classic's OWN single-step companion value, series 5/(1+0.5/1) = 3.3333333333333335 A plus leakage 5/1e7 = 5e-7 A, total 3.3333338333333336 A. Verified empirically by temporarily marking this case portable: the core reports the mathematically exact rule-2a answer instead -- series 5*exp(-0.5) = 3.0326532985631669 A plus the same 5e-7 A leakage, total 3.032653798563167 A (bit-identical to `fixedPairCapacitorCurrentAt(5, 1, 1, 1e7, 0.5)`, test/core/equivalence/analytic.ts) -- which differs from classic's crude one-step approximation by 0.30068 A, about 9% of the expected value and six orders of magnitude past this test's 5e-8 `toBeCloseTo` bound. This is not the load-instant/first-step artifact rule 2a's README bullet documents (that is specific to esr=0); it is classic's own large-step discretisation error at a genuinely non-ideal esr, which the core is BY DESIGN more accurate than. Reclassifying this exact assertion portable would require either the core to reproduce classic's inexact single-step arithmetic (wrong direction for W1b) or loosening this test's own tolerance (which this worker does not own and must not do to force a pass) -- so it stays classic-only, for a materially different reason than before.

cases.describe: 74LS47 — lamp test
cases.name: forces all seven segment outputs LOW when /LT is asserted (LOW)
cases.reason: Lamp-test override forces every segment to sink regardless of the BCD input (core/README.md rule 7's lt_n precedence over the BCD decode); plain load()/step()/getNetV.

cases.describe: 74LS47 — blanking
cases.name: releases all outputs when /RBO is driven LOW externally (blanking input)
cases.reason: /RBO driven LOW releases every segment, but BCD=15 (a=b=c=d=HIGH) is already blank (LS47_SEGMENTS[15]) — a core that ignored rbo_n entirely and always fell through to the BCD decode would pass this case unnoticed. It only proves rbo_n does not break the already-blank case, not that it takes precedence over a real decode. The genuine precedence check (a non-blank BCD forced blank by rbo_n LOW, plus a same-BCD control with rbo_n HIGH) is combinational-ics.test.ts's "gate 1 supplemental — 74LS47 /RBO blanking precedence" describe block (review finding 15).

cases.describe: 74LS47 — blanking
cases.name: zero-suppresses digit 0 when /RBI is LOW
cases.reason: Ripple-blanking input on BCD=0 releases every segment (zero suppression); plain load()/step()/getNetV.

cases.describe: 74LS47 — open control pins (FIX 4: internal pull-ups)
cases.name: decodes BCD digit 5 normally when /LT, /RBI, /RBO are all left unconnected
cases.reason: /LT, /RBI and /RBO left OPEN must resolve HIGH (core/README.md rule 4's OPEN_HIGH pins, IC_OPEN_HIGH_PINS) so the chip decodes normally instead of latching lamp-test or blanking; exercises the open-pin path distinct from the floating-input path (those three pins are OPEN_HIGH, not FLOATING_INPUT).

cases.describe: digital realism — propagation delay
cases.name: holds a 74LS gate output until the package delay has elapsed
cases.reason: After engine.load(circuit), this mutates circuit.components.find(...).params.voltage on the SAME retained JS object WITHOUT calling engine.load() again, relying on classic's load() keeping a live reference (this.circuit = circuit, sim-engine.ts:2445) and re-reading component.params on every subsequent Newton iterate. The core adapter's load() compiles the circuit into a WASM program once; a later in-place mutation of the JS object has no effect on an already-loaded core program (there is no live binding, and Decision 1's toggle mechanism covers only switch/dip 'closed' params, not a voltage_source's voltage). Routing this case through the core would silently keep the OLD input forever and fail its own later assertion (digitalState flipping after the delay) rather than reproduce classic's propagation-delay behaviour — a classic implementation-detail dependency, not a like-for-like core comparison. (The core's own delay-FSM timing is instead proven by the 74ls47 prop_delay_ns case above, which DOES reload.)

cases.describe: gate 1 supplemental — 74HC14 Schmitt inverter: a genuinely observed propagation delay
cases.name: the digital commit lands measurably AFTER 1a crosses the Schmitt threshold — neither immediate (0ns) nor absurdly late (us-scale)

A live RELOAD-based transition (the mechanism wave2-sequential.test.ts's 74HC74 edge tests use) is not usable either: a core reload re-runs decision 8's zero-delay t=0 settle with no per-id carry-forward yet (W2 scope — the same reason this file's own "Schmitt commit semantics"/prop_delay=35ns "not-yet" cases above are not portable), so the new input would commit with NO delay on the core only. This case instead feeds 1a from a plain RC network already present at load time — a genuine continuous analog crossing during ordinary step()s, with no second load() anywhere (the same mechanism fixture 19's relaxation oscillator uses) — and dynamically locates both the analog crossing and the digital commit, asserting the gap between them is bounded to the tens-of-ns ballpark the 15ns catalog value lives in, ruling out both "skipped entirely" and "some unrelated us-scale mechanism".

cases.describe: 74HC74 — D captured on rising edge only
cases.name: D=1 is captured when CLK goes LOW→HIGH (rising edge)
cases.reason: Verified by running against the core: passes. The circuit reloads once (CLK 0V->5V, D unchanged) after settling with CLK LOW for two steps. Before that reload the register is still at its power-on value (Q=0, core/README.md's "Register state" point 2), and the reload's own edge pass runs with lastClk forced to 0 (point 7: "The one edge pass then runs point 5 with every lastClk at 0"), so a clock already reading HIGH at reload is itself a rising edge -- classic's own phantom-edge behaviour, reproduced here. That phantom edge alone reconstructs Q=1 (D=1 captured) with no need to carry any pre-reload state forward, so the W2-scope load-carry-forward gap (no per-id state survives a core reload) is not observable in this specific case.

cases.describe: 74HC74 — async /PRE and /CLR overrides
cases.name: /CLR overrides a previously captured Q=1
cases.reason: Verified by running against the core: passes. Two reloads occur (capture D=1 via the same phantom-edge mechanism as "D=1 is captured", then assert /CLR LOW), but the SECOND reload's assertion depends only on /CLR being asserted -- point 5's asynchronous priority ("/clr 0 -> Q=0, Q1n=1") applies at every evaluation, including the frozen settle pass that runs before any edge (point 7: "the frozen settle drives classic's stamp view of the power-on state, with the live paths live... 74hc74 /pre and /clr"). So /CLR forces Q=0 regardless of whatever the register was reset to at reload -- the load-carry-forward gap is unobservable here because the assertion never depends on the PRE-reload state.

cases.describe: gate 1 supplemental — 74LS173 4-bit D register (tri-state outputs)
cases.name: M HIGH tri-states Q1 (a pull-up shows the float) while the register still holds the loaded D1=LOW
cases.reason: New case (this worker; README point 5, "M and N do not enter the update", and point 8, "the 173 shows its register while M or N tri-states the pins"). M tied HIGH throughout (so Q1 is HIZ from t=0), D1=LOW, G1=G2=LOW so the SAME clock edge that tri-states Q1 also loads D1 into the register underneath; a 10k pull-up to VCC on Q1 would read HIGH whether Q1 is genuinely floating or the pull-up is simply stronger than a driven LOW -- the point of this case is that a driven LOW output overpowers a 10k pull-up (as every other case in this file and combinational-ics.test.ts relies on), so reading Q1 HIGH here specifically shows Q1 is NOT driven, i.e. genuinely tri-stated. Verified by running: netVoltage(q1) > 4V (float, pulled up) while digitalState["u1/q1"] === 0 (the register's true, loaded content).

cases.reason: New case (this worker). /CLR tied active HIGH throughout, D1..D4 all tied HIGH (would load 1111 if /CLR did not override), one RC clock edge. Verified by running: q1..q4 all read LOW after the edge -- /CLR's level override wins over the load, not merely "a load was never attempted".

cases.describe: gate 1 supplemental — 74HC74 divide-by-two from a live 74HC14 relaxation oscillator
cases.name: Q1_n -> D1 (toggle wiring): Q1 flips exactly once per oscillator rising edge, so Q1's own frequency is half the oscillator's
cases.reason: New case (this worker; the brief's "a free-running clock from fixture 19's 74hc14 relaxation oscillator"). The SAME R=10k/C=100nF Schmitt relaxation-oscillator topology as test/fixtures/core/19-74hc14-relaxation-oscillator.sim.json (built inline so its 1Y output can also drive u1.clk1), with Q1_n wired back to D1 (the classic toggle-flip-flop divide-by-two configuration) and /PRE1//CLR1 tied inactive HIGH. Verified by running for 3000 steps of 20us (60ms, several oscillator periods): the oscillator's own 1Y genuinely toggled more than 4 times, and Q1's own digitalState toggle count tracked the oscillator's rising-edge count 1:1 (within +/-1 for the run's start/end boundary) -- a D=Q_bar flip-flop flips its OWN state on every rising clock edge, so its OWN PERIOD (not its toggle count) is twice the clock's, the textbook divide-by-two.

cases.describe: gate 1 supplemental — 74HC74 divide-by-two from a live 74HC14 relaxation oscillator
cases.name: /PRE1 LOW holds Q1 HIGH the whole time, despite a running clock
cases.reason: New case (this worker). Verified by running for 3000 steps: digitalState["u1/q1"]===1 and ["u1/q1_n"]===0 at every single sampled step -- a genuinely live, oscillating clock never manages to flip Q1, proving /PRE1 is a real asynchronous override and not merely "the clock never toggled".

cases.describe: gate 1 supplemental — 74LS189 16x4 RAM (inverted outputs)
cases.name: power-on: mem[addr]=0xF reads back inverted -- /O1../O4 all LOW -- while /CS is LOW and /WE is HIGH
cases.reason: New case (this worker; core/README.md's memories section, 74ls189 State-at-load and Publish points). /CS tied active LOW, /WE tied inactive HIGH, address tied to 0, a 10k pull-up per output pin (so a driven LOW is distinguishable from a floating HIGH). Verified by running: /O1../O4 all read LOW, matching the power-on mem=0xF inverted through all four bits.

cases.describe: gate 1 supplemental — 74LS189 16x4 RAM (inverted outputs)
cases.name: a write through /WE (driven low-to-high by an RC edge) stores D1..D4, then a read shows the new nibble inverted
cases.reason: New case (this worker; the brief's own 74ls189 write case). /CS tied active LOW throughout; address tied to 5 and D1..D4 tied to nibble 6 (0b0110) throughout; /WE fed from a one-shot RC edge starting LOW (the capacitor is uncharged at a fresh load, same fact combinational-ics.test.ts's own 74HC14 case relies on) and rising to HIGH. Per README's 74ls189 write rule ("Write, with edges live only: when csLow && weHigh && lastWE==0, mem[addr]=D... the trailing edge of /we"): /we reads LOW at the load settle, so lastWE settles to 0 there (no phantom write, matching "State at load"'s own no-phantom-write guarantee); the RC node's later LOW->HIGH crossing is then exactly the trailing edge the rule keys on, with the address/data lines already at their final (static) values. Verified by running: after the edge, /O1=HIGH (d1=0), /O2=LOW (d2=1), /O3=LOW (d3=1), /O4=HIGH (d4=0) -- the new nibble, inverted.

cases.describe: gate 1 supplemental — 28C16 EEPROM: a static read of a known byte
cases.name: /OE and /CE LOW, /WE HIGH: IO0..IO7 read back the seeded byte 0x5A at the tied address
cases.reason: New case (this worker; the brief's "a read of a known byte from params.contents at a tied address" -- the write path is D4b's harness job, needing switch stimuli). /OE and /CE tied active LOW, /WE tied inactive HIGH (pure read, no write ever attempted), address tied to 0x100, params.contents base64-encodes a 2048-byte image that is 0xFF everywhere except byte 0x100 = 0x5A. A fully static circuit -- no reload, no live param, no RC edge needed at all for a plain read. Verified by running: IO0..IO7 read back 0x5A's bits exactly (both via getNetV and digitalState).

cases.describe: gate 1 supplemental — 28C256 EEPROM: a static read of a known byte
cases.name: /OE and /CE LOW, /WE HIGH: IO0..IO7 read back the seeded byte 0xC3 at the tied address
cases.reason: New case (this worker). Same mechanism as the 28C16 read case, one address-bit family wider (a0..a14, 15 bits, size 32768) -- needed because gate-reporter.ts's coverage-floor check (finding 9) counts "28c16" and "28c256" as two separate CORE_IMPLEMENTED_KINDS entries, so the 28C16 case alone would leave 28c256 at zero. Address 0x4321, seeded byte 0xC3. Verified by running: IO0..IO7 read back 0xC3's bits exactly.

cases.describe: rgb_led — each channel is its own junction against the common cathode
cases.name: drops its own forward voltage on every channel: blue above green above red

cases.describe: missing_flyback
cases.name: latches at load for an inductor switched by a transistor with no diode across it
cases.reason: W3 (orchestrator ruling, W1g round 2): missing_flyback moves to W3. Every case switches its winding with a W3 transistor (bjt_npn or nmos), so none can join at W1h, whatever the inductor (W1h) or the relay and dc_motor (later waves) do; the diode in some cases is not in the W1 plan's kind table either. The facade path ships in W1g (W1g point 11).
